verdict.summary: Register an API client in your Heroku account settings (name plus callback URL) and any Heroku user can authorize it immediately, with no review and clear read/write scopes. Watch for team admins who turn off third-party OAuth for team-owned apps, and for Heroku's February 2026 move to a 'sustaining engineering' model.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Client registration is a name and callback URL; the flow is standard authorization code with a refresh token.

timeToProd.assumes: An agent using the read or write scopes to inspect or manage apps, dynos and add-ons; read-protected is needed if it must see config vars.
timeToProd.waitingOn: No review needed. Separately, a team admin must not have disabled third-party OAuth for that team's apps.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The OAuth article mentions no review, approval or client limit.

prerequisites.item: A Heroku account (with MFA, which Heroku requires for dashboard access)
prerequisites.why: API clients are registered under an account; the account owns the client ID and secret.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: MFA requirement comes from Heroku's 2023 move away from password API auth; the OAuth article doesn't state it.

prerequisites.why: Users are redirected to the client's redirect URI with code and state after consent.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The article doesn't say whether HTTPS is required.

prerequisites.item: Server-side storage for the client secret and refresh tokens
prerequisites.why: The token and refresh requests send client_secret, and refresh tokens don't expire.

scopeTiers.impact: Read-only access to account information. Enough for 'Sign in with Heroku', nothing else.
Read or write all of the user's apps and resources, excluding account info and config vars. Note: some readable resources, such as log drain URLs, can embed credentials.
Adds runtime secrets such as database connection strings. Needed for an agent that debugs config, but a much bigger trust ask.
Read and write all of the account, apps and resources, the same as the CLI's default authorization. Team-owned authorizations still can't do user-only actions.

steps.title: Sign in to the Heroku dashboard
steps.detail: Use the account (preferably a shared company account) that should own the OAuth client.

steps.title: Register an API client
steps.detail: Account settings → Applications → API Clients → Register New API Client. Enter a name (shown to users on consent) and the callback URL. Alternatively use the CLI oauth plugin or POST /oauth/clients.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The page returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20 (not signed in).

steps.title: Store client ID and secret
steps.detail: Copy the ID and secret into your secret manager.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Map agent features to scopes: read for inspection, write for scaling/restarts, read-protected only if config vars are needed.

steps.title: Implement authorize redirect
steps.detail: Redirect to https://id.heroku.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&response_type=code&scope=read&state=<csrf>. 'code' is the only supported response_type.

steps.title: Implement token exchange and refresh
steps.detail: POST grant_type=authorization_code&code=...&client_secret=... to https://id.heroku.com/oauth/token. Store refresh_token; refresh with grant_type=refresh_token before the 8-hour access token expires.

steps.title: Call the Platform API
steps.detail: Send Authorization: Bearer HRKU-... and Accept: application/vnd.heroku+json; version=3 to https://api.heroku.com (for example GET /apps). Track RateLimit-Remaining.

steps.title: Test with a team-owned app
steps.detail: Authorize from a second account that belongs to a Heroku team, and confirm team apps are visible. If not, the team admin may have turned off third-party OAuth in the team's Settings tab.

agentCanDo: Write the authorize, callback and refresh code
Register the client via POST /oauth/clients once given a token
Write help text for team admins about third-party OAuth settings
humanMustDo: Sign in (with MFA) and register the API client
Ask customers' team admins to allow third-party OAuth if needed

blockers.cause: Invalid, expired or reused code, or wrong client_secret.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code once, promptly, with the matching client's secret.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed with dummy values on 2026-10-20; we couldn't separate the causes.

blockers.symptom: API calls start failing about 8 hours after connect
blockers.cause: Access tokens expire 8 hours after issue (expires_in 28799).
blockers.fix: Refresh with the stored refresh_token, which doesn't expire.

blockers.symptom: User authorizes successfully but team-owned apps are missing or forbidden
blockers.cause: Team admins can deny OAuth access to team-owned resources from all non-Heroku products in the team's Settings tab.
blockers.fix: Ask the team admin to re-enable third-party OAuth access to the Platform API.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error returned in this case wasn't documented.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with id rate_limit
blockers.cause: Each account has a 4,500-token pool refilled at about 75/min; your agent shares it with the user's other tools.
blockers.fix: Back off, check RateLimit-Remaining or GET /account/rate-limits (free), and cache reads.

blockers.symptom: Config vars come back empty or forbidden
blockers.cause: The read and write scopes exclude configuration variables.
blockers.fix: Request read-protected or write-protected, and explain why on your consent copy.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after 8 hours; refresh tokens don't expire. Tokens are 65 characters and prefixed HRKU-, which helps secret scanners.
Rate limits are per account, not per OAuth client, so heavy use by your agent eats into the user's own CLI and tool budget.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The reference describes a per-account pool and doesn't mention per-client pools.

nuances.text: Even read and read-protected tokens can expose write credentials embedded in metadata, such as log drain URLs. Treat stored tokens as highly sensitive.
Users and admins can revoke an authorization (DELETE /oauth/authorizations/{id}), which blocks its tokens immediately; build reconnect handling.
Since 16 February 2026, Heroku may make breaking changes to production API resources with three months' notice in the Changelog instead of a new API version. Watch the changelog.

On 6 February 2026 Heroku announced a move to a 'sustaining engineering model' focused on stability rather than new features, and stopped offering new enterprise contracts. Weigh this if Heroku is core to your product.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Read via Simon Willison's link post, which quotes Heroku's own announcement.

nuances.text: No OIDC discovery document is published at id.heroku.com, so use the identity scope and GET /account for user info.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: https://id.heroku.com/.well-known/openid-configuration returned a 'Page Not Found' HTML page on 2026-10-20.
